crest-whitestrips.text: Users apply these strips over a one-to-three-week course to brighten their smile, and clinical trials report lightening of a shade or two. The change in tooth colour is visible and measurable, and it is one of the most widely used at-home whitening options.

custom-bleaching-trays.text: Dentist-fitted trays are used at home to lighten teeth with carbamide peroxide gel, and are a long-standing alternative to strips. The whitening is a visible change in tooth shade, and the method has been described in dental literature since the late 1980s.

whitening-mouth-rinse.text: People use peroxide mouthwashes as a low-effort way to lighten tooth colour and reduce stain over weeks. Results are described as gradual, taking up to a few months, and the supporting evidence is mainly laboratory work.

chain: Whiter teeth over a full course
potassium-nitrate-desensitising-toothpas.text: Whitening users reach for this toothpaste to ease the sensitivity that often comes with peroxide bleaching, so they can complete a course and reach a brighter smile. It has been studied for dentine pain in general, not for whitening outcomes specifically.

prophy-paste-polish.text: Dental hygienists use this polishing paste to lift surface stain during a cleaning, leaving teeth looking cleaner and smoother. Appearance communities discuss it for stain removal; the research on it focuses on abrasivity and materials rather than cosmetic results.

lip-suction-pump.text: Users place the cup over the lips to make them look fuller, and the swelling is visible within minutes. The effect is temporary, and no studies of these devices were found.

chain: Ears of typical shape and position
earwell-infant-ear-molding.text: Parents and clinicians use this splinting system in the first weeks of life to reshape congenital ear differences such as lop or prominent ears without surgery. Clinical reports are consistently positive but lack controlled comparisons.

dermastamp-0-5mm.text: Forum users press this stamp onto skin and brows to boost topical absorption and soften fine lines, and some report it helps minoxidil on brows. Microneedling has been studied for skin texture and scars; the brow, eye-line and orbital-fat claims rest on anecdote.

red-light-mask-omnilux-currentbody.text: Users wear these LED masks regularly in pursuit of fewer wrinkles, clearer skin and less puffiness. Red-light therapy has been studied for skin ageing and acne with mixed, often preliminary results, and consumer masks are less studied than clinical devices.

chain: Red and near-infrared light on skin
photorejuvenation-led-panel.text: Users aim these home LED panels at the face or body for fine lines, texture, acne and hair growth. The mechanism is proposed from lab and clinical-device studies, while trials of consumer panels are limited.

ultrasound-scaler-home.text: Appearance communities discuss home scalers as a way to remove visible tartar and stain between dental visits. Research covers professional ultrasonic scalers; home units have not been studied the same way.

1-testosterone-1-test-dihydroboldenone.text: Sold online as a prohormone supplement, it was used by bodybuilders seeking muscle size and a bigger physique. It has been a controlled substance in the US since 2005, and there are no human trials of its effects.

methyl-1-testosterone-m1t.text: An oral designer androgen sold in early-2000s supplements aimed at bodybuilders chasing muscle size. Evidence for the muscle-building use is anecdotal, with animal work and a kidney-injury case report as the main published material.

methylstenbolone-m-sten-hybrid.text: Sold online as a supplement or research chemical, it is used by lifters seeking muscle gain and a harder physique. It has never been trialled in people; published human material is a case report of cholestatic jaundice.

methyldienolone-methyldienolone-m-dien.text: An unmarketed oral 19-nor androgen that appears in bodybuilding discussion as a muscle-building compound. Almost nothing is published beyond detection chemistry, so its muscle effect in people is untested.

dimethyltrienolone-dimethyltren-ru-2420.text: A never-marketed trenbolone analog that comes up in bodybuilding circles for its reported animal potency, said to be far above methyltestosterone. No human data exist, so its muscle-building use is speculative.

metribolone-r1881-methyltrienolone.text: Best known as a laboratory standard for androgen receptor studies, it was dropped as a drug and appears in doping cases and underground muscle-building talk. Its use for physique goals is based on anecdote rather than trials.

tetrahydrogestrinone-thg-the-clear.text: The 2003 designer steroid made to evade doping tests, taken by athletes for muscle and performance. It is potent in laboratory assays and has never been studied in people.

desoxymethyltestosterone-dmt-madol.text: A 1960s oral steroid revived as a designer doping agent and supplement ingredient for muscle gain. The evidence is limited to animal data, with no human trials of the physique use.

prostanozol.text: A designer prohormone sold in bodybuilding supplements to deliver a stanozolol-like effect for lean muscle. It is now a Schedule III substance in the US and has no clinical data.

methyldiazinol.text: A 1965 laboratory curiosity with a high reported animal muscle-to-androgen ratio, which is the basis of any interest in it for muscle building. It was never marketed and nothing else is on record.

epistane-epitiostanol-derivative-havoc.text: Sold online as a supplement since about 2009, it is used by lifters who want a harder, leaner muscular look. Nobody has trialled it, and case reports link it to liver bile-flow problems.

methoxydienone-methoxy-18-methyl.text: A nandrolone-family steroid from contraceptive research that surfaced as a designer supplement for muscle building. No human trials exist for that use.

bolandione.text: A nandrolone prohormone sold over the counter in the US until 2005 for muscle gain. It is now controlled and best known for causing doping-test positives; human evidence for the physique effect is thin.

19-nor-4-androstenedione-19-norandrosten.text: Sold as an over-the-counter nandrolone prohormone in the US until 2005, used by bodybuilders for muscle gain. Today it is mostly a doping-control footnote, with little evidence on the physique use.

trendione.text: A trenbolone metabolite sold online as a prohormone-type supplement for muscle and a harder look. It has been studied mostly in cattle-manure environmental research, not in people.

dienedione.text: Marketed as a trenbolone-type prohormone supplement for muscle gain until it was scheduled in 2010. No human studies exist for its muscle effects.

4-androstenediol-4-ad.text: An early-2000s oral prohormone marketed to raise testosterone and support muscle growth. The muscle claims were large, and human evidence for them is limited.

1-androsterone-1-andro.text: A designer DHEA-type prohormone sold online as a dietary supplement for muscle gain. It is known from seizure and doping-detection papers, with no human trials.

chain: Less fat stored, more lean mass
adrenosterone-11-keto-androstenedione.text: Sold as '11-OXO' for fat loss and a leaner physique, with the pitch resting on a proposed cortisol-blocking mechanism. It is a natural adrenal steroid, but supplement trials in people are lacking.
